REYES Sangguniang Bayan (SB) Member Municipality of Looc, Romblon Dear SB Member Reyes: DILG Legal opinion No. 15, S. 2014 22 APR 2014 This refers to your undated letter which requests this level's opinion or clarification on the implementation of Local Budget Circular No. 103 (LBC 103), dated 13 May 2013, particularly on the interpretation of Items 7.1 and 7.5 thereof. The following are the factual allegations in your letter: The Municipality of Looc, Romblon implemented LBC 103 beginning January 2013. Following said implementation, the Municipal Accountant deducted P2,800.00 per absence from the respective representation and transportation allowance (RATA) of the SB Members, citing Items 7.1 and 7.5 of LBC 103. When asked, the Municipal Accountant allegedly explained that one (1) absence from regular sessions Of the SB Member is equivalent to one (I) week since the SB is required to hold one (1) regular session every week, or four (4) times a month under Republic Act No. 7160 (hereinafter, the "Code"). It is your contention that while it is true that the Sanggunian is required to hold session once a week or four (4) times a month, it does not mean that their duties anå responsibilities is limited to attending sessions. Hence, the request. Local Budget Circular No. 1031, dated 15 May 2013, provides a different manner of computing the Representation and Transportation Allowance (RAT A) for government officials observing an eight-hour work day (Item 7.1, LBC 103) vis-å-vis those officials, who by the nature of their official functions, adopt a work schedule other than the usual eight hours per day, forty hours per week schedule (Item 7.5, LBC 103), viz: "7.0 General Guidelines on the Grant of the RATA 7.1 A rationalized scheme on the grant of RATA based on the number Of days of actual work performance on workdays by the I Amended Rules and Regulations on the Grant of Representation and Transportation Allowances

o , al concerned is hereby prescribed. The RAA schedule follows: Number of Workdays Of Actual Work Performance in a Month I to 5 6 toll 12 to 16 17 and more Actual RATA for a month 25% the RATA 500/00 the monthl RATA 750/00 the monthl RATA 1000/00 the monthl RATA xxx 7.5 For Officials who, by the nature of their official functions, adopt a work schedule other than the usual eight hours per day, forty hours per week, such as the members of the local sanggunian, RATA shall be ro-rated based on the actual wor attendance o the Qficial vis-å-vis the work schedule or perfprmance standards prescribed by law or by competent authority, following the schedule below: Percentage of Actual Work/A ttendance in Relation to a Full Monthly Work Schedu Ie 25% or less 260/0-500/0 51%-750/0 750/0-1000/0 Actual RATA for a month 250/00 the monthl RATA 500/00 the monthl RATA 750/00 the monthl RATA 1000/00 the monthl RATA Based on the foregoing, Members of the local sanggunian belong to the second class of government offcials, hence, are governed by Item 7.5 of LBC 103. Notably, Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991, does not prescribe the work schedule or performance standards for local elective officials. However, Section 50 thereof provides that the local sanggunian may adopt or update its existing internal rules of procedure (IRP). It is this Department's opinion that the local sanggunian falls within the purview Of "competent authority," as mentioned in Item 7.5 of I BC 103. As such, local sanUunians may adopt/prescribe in its IRP rules governing the performance standards of members thereof. Anent the work schedule of elective officials, in Macatangay vs. The Chairman of the Commission on Audit2, the Supreme Court took judicial notice of the fact that elective 2 G.R. No. 1„-38728. 30 September 1982

officials rendition o . vice does not follow a certain or defimte work schedule as they are deemed in service of their constituents regardless of time and place, viz.: "What was said in the Memorandum for Respondent is relevant: "As a general proposition, elective officials' entitlement to salary is not dependent upon actual attendance in office. In fact, they are not even required to keep record of their daily attendance such as by accomplishing Civil Service Form No. 48 (Daily Time Record) or punching the bundy clock. Thus, a provincial governor is entitled to collect salary even when absent on a personal business, it being well-settled that an elected Officer is entitled to emoluments so long as he is permitted to retain the office, the right thereto being independent of services performed. (Op., Insular Auditor, Dec. 23, 1919, cited in Araneta, the Adm. Code, Vol. I V, pp. 2720, 2721). Elective officials, indeedz are deemed in the service Of their constituents regardless of time and place. There can be no occasion to consider them absent from work since their presence at such specified time and place is not a pre-requisite to their collection of salary for services rendered. So, too, they need not seek leave to be absentfor there is no absence to speak Of. "[Emphasis and underscoring supplied] Verily, the work performed by members of local is not limited or confined to attendance during sessions. In view of the foregoing, it would be erroneous to solely set the attendance of sanggunian members during regular sessions as their work schedule or regard the same as a performance standard as their duties and responsibilities are not confined to attendance during sessions. Moreover, it should be emphasized that only the legislature or a competent authority can prescribe the work schedule or performance standards of sanggunian members. We hope the foregoing sufficiently addressed your concern. Very truly yours, AUSTERE A. ANAD RO Undersecretary 08 @ DILG-OUSLG 2014-04-01 cxu
